population.text: Compiled program begins with an absolute bytecode jump to the new-session path at $298C. The helper immediately following checks protection markers.

Define the random-index helper and unpack high scores. Demo state selects attract setup; otherwise run difficulty/player menus, restore the selected player account and enter level loading.

Restore player lives/score, disable game interrupts, and derive disk level from difficulty base plus round. Mystery clears round and uses base & 127; values above 39 invoke FN30. Pass zero-based level through FB and call level load. LOAD accepts status $40. FIRE retries can reach a fourth LOAD, but the counter>2 check at $2A1A aborts before testing even a successful fourth status. The no-FIRE wait at $2A34 does not advance its timeout counter.

Show Disk Error and wait for FIRE. The fractional counter increment at $2A7A runs once; the back edge $2AAB returns to $2A84, skipping that increment. From the ordinary zeroed retry counter it does not time out to the title. Original-code testing observes 10000 polls; a live missing-file test observes 600 PAL frames with 8049 wait-entry reads and no increment-opcode reads. The counter remains unchanged in both, and FIRE returns with counter 1. Do not confuse this with the score-save timeout at $4851.

Check protection, initialize variable/register aliases and HUD; level index 37 calls $7030 to black out playfield colors. Reset start position, materialize the player and set difficulty from the selected base before the main update loop.

Compute delay = 4*(9-speed)^1.15 + 2 - 2*(speed==9), where a true compiled comparison is -1. Thus speed 9 gives delay 4. Update player, process exit/spell events or death; otherwise delay and update six actors.

Compiled death gate: reached only after nonzero $C02A, unless active $C035 travel cleared it. Sprite-7 color 2 bypasses Invisibility. Otherwise nonzero V21 suppresses this fatal report, clears $C02A and enters $30B3; safe movement passes do not spend V21. Original interpreter matrix: 84 states; safe passes, all 32 protected reports and the next death checked live.

Save spell color/base/animation, initialize effect velocity and lifetime from player height, substitute shape $DD, and adjust loop delay for the selected speed. Enable sprite 6 for the falling/bouncing effect.

Update actors, wait and animate the wizard death while checking effect height/terrain. Offer the remaining teleport/fall/levitate spell escape when a charge remains, otherwise restore saved spell graphics and settle score/lives.

Restore spell descriptor, temporarily suppress completion bonus while reading HUD score, deduct one life and update HUD. Restart a surviving player on this level; with no lives clear bonus and advance turns. Live two-player probes: 2 lives becomes 1 and retries player 1; 1 life becomes 0 and restores player 2 with six lives. Score 2000 is retained on the surviving retry.
Spend a charge, remove the death effect sprite, set cast latch, invoke teleport/feather-fall/levitate engine entry according to spell ID and resume normal play with recomputed delay.
Clear status area and print the six-cell bonus caption/bar template before shared player/level/speed HUD drawing.
Print player number, one-based level, score caption, remaining spell charges and speed. Reset facing and import live lives count from $C008.
Print charge and score fields, render current spell name, right-align the saved score using its decimal digit count, replace field spaces with zeroes and draw up to ten life icons.
Clear exit event, convert HUD score and remaining bonus into player account values, then join turn progression.
Event bit 7 means level completion. Otherwise mask spell ID and dispatch: IDs 1-4 have no script action; 5 invisibility, 6 teleport, 7 feather fall, 8 levitate, 9 haste, 10 slow.
Set V21=32, set sprite-7 color to background $D021 and clear its multicolor bit. V21 counts protected fatal reports, not elapsed movement passes. Red hazard-death state bypasses protection at $2B6E.

Consume one V21 unit after a suppressed fatal report. Restore sprite-7 multicolor at 16; below 9 set color from 10-V21/3; at zero set color 4. Continuous danger can spend units on successive movement updates. Live sequence agrees with original compiled interpreter.

Compiled spell handler: arm cast latch, clear event and SYS $7075 to set coordinate-exchange effect 1. The first target is the level start; later targets are remembered departure coordinates. $79B3 adds a random-direction two-pixel horizontal nudge after exchanging positions.
Compiled spell handler sets cast latch and SYS $7063: effect 6 descends two pixels per player update, bypassing ordinary gravity until terrain ends the effect.
Compiled spell handler sets cast latch and SYS $7069: effect 4 ascends two pixels per player update until terrain ends the effect.
Replace shared loop delay with delay/2+1. The same main loop still updates player and actors; the script changes delay rather than a separate player velocity.
Set cast latch, reduce actor horizontal pursuit speeds to +1/-1 and increase loop delay by one when its old value is below 64.
Player number 1-6 indexes lives at $02BF+player and a 24-bit score split across $02C5/$02CB/$02D1+player. Reconstruct score and copy lives into $C008.

Initialize scalar aliases for VIC $D000, SID $D400, sprite pointers $C7F8, events $C02A, actor support $C03D and level header $C300. Clear per-level temporaries and define helper functions before clearing actor sprite pointers.
Define FN descriptor $2954. Its body saves/restores local V2 and returns player low X plus 256 when D010 bit 7 is set, using BASIC true=-1 in the arithmetic.
Define FN $295E: return the selected VIC register with bits in the current V18 mask removed. Save and restore the function argument local.
Zero sprite pointers 0-6 after defining the helper functions, leaving wizard slot 7 for player setup.
Initialize menu/session values and SID/VIC appearance; print the six choices Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert, Customized and Mystery, with joystick/FIRE instructions.
Animate arrows and row colors, read port-2 direction/FIRE, wrap selection between 0 and 5, and restart title after inactivity. FIRE highlights the chosen text and waits for release.

Show the player-count prompt and initialize count one. Each new directional press increments it; comparison with seven adds -6, wrapping six back to one. FIRE accepts, with warning sounds and title return on timeout. Live: five joystick edges from one player select six, confirmed by menu text and scalar value.
Wait for FIRE release, show speed-key instructions (nine quickest) and wait for the final press. Inactivity returns to the title; accepted input clears the prompt and prints publisher footer.

Convert difficulty choice to base 0,10,20,30 or40; Mystery encodes a time-derived random start with bit7 set. Clear round, set all six life slots to six and all eighteen score bytes to zero, then show Player 1 ready.

Clamp negative lives to zero, write lives and three score bytes back to the selected player account. Demo mode retains a life. Call the game-over animation for an eliminated player and seek the next surviving player. Called after completion or final-life loss; a surviving death retries without entering this settlement. Live account probes preserve score 123450, skip eliminated accounts, and advance the round only when wrapping the player list.
Increment player number, skip empty life slots, show Get Ready and return to ordinary level loading or demo setup.

Stop demo mode, sum surviving accounts and end the session when none remain. Otherwise advance round; after ten completed levels show the bonus screen. Mystery chooses another random level before continuing.

Clear bonus and transient effects, configure five sprite shapes/positions and SID voices for the game-over scene. First raise the four expanded letter/character sprites into view, then prepare a passing effect sprite.

Dissolve the fifth sprite, animate another sprite across nine-bit X=0..328 in four-pixel steps, alter pitches and dissolve each crossed letter at its trigger position. End by disabling sprites and horizontal expansion.
Read level header start Y, even-align low X by INT(X/2)*2, and restore the level X-high mask into VIC registers.
Disable game interrupts and congratulate the player after ten levels. Every surviving account receives INT(difficulty_base/10+2) extra wizards, reduced modulo 256; display the updated status table.

List each selected player with remaining wizards or DEAD inside a text frame. Wait for FIRE or a loop-count timeout; reset round and increase difficulty base by ten, changing base40 to Mystery flag128.

Disable game interrupts. Ordinary play updates aggregate statistics and ranks scores; demo skips score submission. The shared display path draws a bordered high-score screen.
Print the rank labels, copy three initials columns and display ten stored scores multiplied by 50. The top rank additionally shows a sixteen-character full name and wizard sprite.

Continuation of the high-score display bytecode region beginning $3F38, across the fixed $4000 ledger edge. Print stored ranks, initials and scaled scores; opcode-by-opcode side comments carry the exact operations.
Fetch the packed numeric top-score element, compute its decimal width, print value*50 and position a wizard sprite beside the leader. Show the continue prompt.
Wait in fixed delay units for joystick activity or timeout; timeout is shorter in demo mode. Require input release, play confirmation sound and return to title when appropriate.

Clear ten player-attribution flags, reconstruct each player score, divide by 50 and insert before the first strictly lower entry. A tie can enter below an equal score when a lower entry remains. This is numeric insertion only: the separate attribution pass at $42A5 can assign names to pre-existing equal entries. Shift six disk-table columns and the working numeric array down to make room.

Finish numeric insertion, then match each nonzero player score to the first unclaimed equal entry and call name/initials input. This does not track which entry that player inserted: a champion tie can replace the champion name, and a bottom-rank tie can replace initials without numeric insertion. Live top/bottom ties and a six-player prepared ranking confirm the prompts, flags, fields and saved records. Then print final scores in player order.

Position each final-score row, choose alternating reverse text and one of six colors, and print the unscaled player score. Wait for FIRE/timeout, update statistics, then save and display the rankings.
Delay/poll FIRE with a 75-iteration timeout, reset border/background, wait for button release and enter high-score save/display.

Play confirmation and animate the entering player. The top rank additionally requests a full name. Draw a small input frame, call SYS $7078 for three initials and copy them into three ten-entry columns at $C100/$C10A/$C114.

Prompt for up to sixteen letters, draw a nineteen-by-three border, call the timeout-enabled champion-name entry via SYS $706F ($8FB5), then copy sixteen screen cells from $C574 to the SCOR name field at $C13C. The untimed $8FC4 entry belongs to construction-title editing.
Print the nine rank names below Wizard: Sorcerer, Warlock, Necromancer, Magician, Druid, Enchanter, Conjurer, Acolyte and Apprentice.
Define FN $294F: save argument V2, read engine random byte at events+7 ($C031), divide by 256, multiply by requested count and truncate to an index from zero up to count-1.
Read ten three-byte little-endian score values from split SCOR columns $C11E/$C128/$C132 and store them as the five-byte working numeric array at $291D.

Split the ten working scores into three byte columns. Save when any player-attribution flag exists, including a tie that only replaces initials. Nonzero FB shows DISK ERROR: FIRE retries, with at most three SAVE calls; no FIRE increments the fractional counter until it exceeds 2 and returns. Original-code branches and live unavailable-device error/recovery and no-FIRE expiry are checked. FB zero skips the error path but does not guarantee disk persistence; see $8B1E.

Choose ordinary/custom statistic pair by difficulty_base>=40, add selected player count into the low byte and propagate carry into its paired high byte at $C15C-$C15F.

Disable ordinary sprites/sound, choose three special shapes and fixed colors, place them at X=138,164,190, then animate their Y positions from zero through 66 with descending SID pitch before showing the player-number prompt.
Decrement demo selection. If it reaches zero return; otherwise reset one player with one life and zero score, copy the selected resident demonstration level/input stream via SYS $7033 and return.
Two END bytecodes terminate the compiled image; the loader reports the first byte after them as $4A89.
